Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund, distributed automatically to the identified members, with $7 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fee amount the court does not award would go to the class. We are open to discussing the amounts, but automatic distribution is important given Brightline’s records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree automatic distribution is appropriate given the available records. Your proposal exceeds our settlement authority. We can offer a $30 million class fund plus $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Any reduction in approved fees would benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic distribution and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can narrow the gap: $33 million for the class, with your proposed $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval. All other terms remain as you proposed.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic payments and directing any unawarded fees to the class. To narrow the remaining gap, Brightline offers a $31 million class fund plus $6 million in fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with the other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement. We can resolve the remaining gap at a $32 million class fund, with $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval. Payments would be automatic, and any fees not awarded would go to the class. We would not request a clear-sailing provision.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. Brightline can offer a $31.5 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses, for a $37.5 million total, with automatic payments, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We hope this resolves the remaining difference.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $31.5 million class fund with automatic payments, plus $6 million in fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We look forward to preparing the settlement for court review.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery and automatic payments. Keep fees separate, subject to court approval, and direct any fee reduction to the class. The opening amount leaves room to negotiate without sacrificing distribution quality.
Their $43 million proposal exceeds the $40 million authorization. Counter at $36 million total, preserving automatic distribution and court-friendly fee terms.

The $30 million automatic-distribution fund is a credible offer given trial and certification risks. With five rounds remaining, a modest counter may improve class recovery without jeopardizing the key distribution and fee-reversion terms.

The latest $39 million proposal is within authority and has court-approval-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay with four rounds remaining. Counter at $37 million while retaining automatic distribution and class-directed unawarded fees.

The $31 million automatic-distribution fund is a strong offer, but the $2 million gap from our last proposal is narrow and four rounds remain. Seek a modest increase without changing the agreed distribution or fee terms.

The latest $38 million total is within authority and has strong approval prospects. With three rounds remaining, a modest counteroffer may save $500,000 without changing the agreed distribution and fee protections.

Accept. The $31.5 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million probability-weighted trial award even before certification risk, delay, and costs. The separately paid $6 million fee remains subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: As interim class counsel, Hargrove Lane LLP supports preliminary approval. Counsel negotiated the class recovery and attorneys’ fees in parallel, not sequentially. The agreement provides a $31.5 million class fund, with payments sent automatically to the approximately 400,000 identifiable members, and up to $6 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the court does not award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline. The proposed recovery is substantial in light of the risks of class certification and trial, the possibility of no recovery, and the time required to reach judgment. This statement does not disclose confidential mediation offers; counsel can provide further information if the court directs an appropriate procedure.
